## Fixed-boundary rhombic square: even a large original bulk defect cannot force diameter descent

For any integer `m>=2` and any `theta in (pi/3,pi/2)`, take `Q_m={iu+jv:0<=i,j<=m}` with the same unit vectors `u,v`. This set is original unit-separated and triangle-free; every original site with `1<=i,j<=m-1` has a six-positive-facet original full Voronoi cell with area `sin(theta)>a`.

Fix ALL sites for which `i=0` or `i=m` or `j=0` or `j=m`, and allow arbitrary moves of interior sites. Two opposite fixed corners are distance `m|u+v|`, which equals `diam(Q_m)` because the parallelogram's longer diagonal is `u+v` when `theta<pi/2`. Therefore **no boundary-fixed surgery, however large, can strictly decrease the diameter**.

There is also a local isolation estimate. If each moving original site has displacement `d_(i,j)` with `M=max|d_(i,j)|`, maintaining separation at least one along every originally unit `u` or `v` edge gives `u dot(d_(i+1,j)-d_(i,j))>=-2M^2` and the corresponding `v` bound. Summing across horizontal and vertical rows from both pinned ends gives `|u dot d_(i,j)|<=2m M^2` and `|v dot d_(i,j)|<=2m M^2`. The least singular value of the matrix with rows `u^T,v^T` is `sqrt(1-cos(theta))>=1/sqrt(2)`; at a maximally moved site,

`M/sqrt(2) <= 2sqrt(2)*m*M^2`, so `M=0` or `M>=1/(4m)`.

Both conclusions concern **pinned boundary** only and cannot be transferred to arbitrary boundary-free globally optimal configurations. The boundary obstruction is elementary and related to Popper/Carver's previously archived pinned-row result. One part of the Ohm review asserted that the fixed endpoints of every unit-edge row force **every** interior site to stay exactly fixed at all displacement magnitudes. **ROOT rejects this argument:** the triangle inequality only gives `sum edge lengths >= distance between endpoints =m`, which is consistent with longer bent or stretched edges. For example, moving a single interior point arbitrarily far away while all other original points, including the boundary, remain fixed preserves all separations `>=1` once it is far enough, although this increases diameter. The valid `M>=1/(4m)` local-isolation claim is retained, with no global rigidity claim.

Ohm supplied an independently valid **free-boundary descent**: for `0<t<pi/2-theta`, increase `theta` to `theta+t`, replace each original site `iu+jv(theta)` by `iu+jv(theta+t)`, and preserve separation `>=1` for all lattice differences. Then `diam(Q_m(t))=2m*cos((theta+t)/2)<2m*cos(theta/2)` strictly. The displacement is at most `mt` and can be arbitrarily small. Hence **each Q_m is strictly non-optimal even locally when the original boundary can move**. This refutes transferring its boundary-pinned rigidity to the unrestricted objective.

## Independent ROOT audit of a public E0099 zero-gap observation

The publicly accessible `erdosproblems.ai` page *Exact optimizers and finite geometric obstructions*, section E0099, updated October 17, 2026, **credits Plasma AI**, expressly disclaims novelty and independent external review, and records the following observation:

> For each fixed `n>=3`, the infimum of the diameter over feasible original-unit-triangle-free planar configurations is precisely `D_n`.

Source: https://erdosproblems.ai/wiki/research/distance_multiplicity_interfaces/exact_optimizers . This is a distinct externally recorded antecedent, **not** a ROOT-originated theorem or a solution.

ROOT independently reconstructs its short complete proof and a slight exact-density strengthening. Fix any feasible exact global minimizer `X=(x_1,...,x_n)` with minimum original separation one and diameter `D_n`. In the real coordinate space `R^(2n)`, for each distinct pair of unordered pairs `{i,j}!={k,l}` consider the nonzero polynomial

`F_{ij,kl}(Y)=|y_i-y_j|^2-|y_k-y_l|^2`.

Each is a genuine nonzero polynomial in the free coordinates; there are only finitely many. Their zero sets have empty interior. The complement of their finite union is open and dense and contains dense rational-coordinate points. Therefore for every `epsilon>0` one can take a distinct-point **rational** coordinate perturbation `Y` arbitrarily close to `X` with all pairwise distances **different**, minimum separation `m(Y)>0`, and

`diam(Y)/m(Y) < D_n+epsilon`.

Rescale all sites by exactly `1/m(Y)`. The resulting configuration `Z` has minimum original separation **exactly one**, has **exactly one** original pair at distance one, contains **no** unit equilateral triple, and `D_n<=diam(Z)<D_n+epsilon`. Because `Y` has rational coordinates, `m(Y)^2` is a positive rational and `Z` has algebraic coordinates; no floating-point approximation is required for the existence argument. Hence, for **every fixed `n>=3`**,

`inf_{Z feasible, EXACTLY ONE original unit-contact pair} diam(Z) = D_n`.

This strengthens the displayed triangle-free infimum identity's formulation but follows immediately from the same public genericity argument. It does **not** create an exact globally optimal triangle-free `Z`, much less an infinite sequence of such globally optimal `Z`. It proves that **no strictly positive** (even `n`-dependent) diameter gap separates all triangle-free feasible configurations from `D_n`. Any proposed method asserting such a gap without an additional exact-global restriction is false. The earlier Wave124 detached-K3 additive-constant construction is a different restricted geometry statement and retains Bernoulli priority.

### 1\. Exact first-order condition for every global minimizer

Let \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\) be an original unit-separated configuration with globally minimum diameter \(D=D_n\). Define its active pairs:

\[
U=\{ij:\|x_i-x_j\|=1\},\qquad
F=\{ij:\|x_i-x_j\|=D\}.
\]

For each \(ij\in U\), let \(u_{ij}=x_i-x_j\). For each \(ij\in F\), let \(v_{ij}=(x_i-x_j)/D\). These are unit vectors.

Apply an arbitrary small affine deformation \(I+tH\), then rescale to restore minimum separation one. Exact global optimality implies, for every symmetric \(2\times2\) matrix \(H\),

\[
\max_{ij\in F}v_{ij}^{T}Hv_{ij}
\;\ge\;
\min_{ij\in U}u_{ij}^{T}Hu_{ij}.
\]

By convex separation, this is equivalent to the necessary condition

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{conv}\{v_{ij}v_{ij}^{T}:ij\in F\}
\cap
\operatorname{conv}\{u_{ij}u_{ij}^{T}:ij\in U\}
\ne\varnothing .
}
\tag{1}
\]

Thus some probability weights \(\alpha_{ij}\) on diameter pairs and \(\beta_{ij}\) on exact unit contacts satisfy

\[
\sum_{F}\alpha_{ij}v_{ij}v_{ij}^{T}
=
\sum_U\beta_{ij}u_{ij}u_{ij}^{T}.
\tag{2}
\]

This is an exact, finite-dimensional test. It requires no differentiability assumption on the diameter or minimum-distance function.

It is weaker than the complete vertex-by-vertex Karush–Kuhn–Tucker equilibrium already investigated in the project, but is easier to test independently.

### 2\. Quantitative obstruction for the oblique nearhex lattice

Consider

\[
u=(1,0),\qquad
v=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta),\qquad
\frac{\pi}{3}<\theta<\frac{\pi}{2},
\]

and the lattice \(\Lambda_\theta=\mathbb Zu+\mathbb Zv\).

Its **only exact unit-contact directions** are \(\pm u,\pm v\). The contact graph is bipartite and has no \(K_3\). Nevertheless, every sufficiently interior original Voronoi cell has six genuine facets, corresponding to

\[
\pm u,\quad\pm v,\quad\pm(u-v).
\]

The last pair is slightly longer than one:

\[
\|u-v\|=2\sin(\theta/2)>1.
\]

The full-cell area is

\[
A_{\rm cell}=\sin\theta
=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}
+\frac12\left(\theta-\frac\pi3\right)
+O\!\left((\theta-\pi/3)^2\right).
\]

Consequently, choosing \(\theta-\pi/3\) arbitrarily small produces arbitrarily small positive area defects while retaining **zero exact unit triangles**.

There is also a useful new quantitative consequence of (1). If all exact contact directions lie in the two lines generated by \(u,v\), every contact-direction moment matrix has the form

\[
M=p\,uu^T+(1-p)\,vv^T,\qquad 0\le p\le1.
\]

A direct determinant calculation gives

\[
\boxed{
\min_{0\le p\le1}
\left\|M-\frac12I\right\|_F
=\frac{|\cos\theta|}{\sqrt2}.
}
\tag{3}
\]

For \(\theta\) near \(60^\circ\), this lower bound approaches \(1/(2\sqrt2)\approx0.35355\).

**Interpretation:** a globally optimal configuration whose unit-contact directions belong to this nearhex two-line pattern must admit a substantially anisotropic diameter-direction stress. If its diameter-pair moment matrices cannot supply that anisotropy, (1) disproves global optimality.

This is a concrete, falsifiable obstruction. It does **not** yet eliminate oblique lattices: an almost circular hull need not force an isotropic choice of diameter stress.

### 3\. Why localized site movements fail

The oblique lattice also defeats straightforward one-site perturbations. A bulk center has four exact unit neighbors at \(\pm u,\pm v\). If its displacement \(d\) preserves separation from those fixed neighbors, then

\[
|u\cdot d|\le \frac{\|d\|^2}{2},
\qquad
|v\cdot d|\le \frac{\|d\|^2}{2}.
\]

Since \(u,v\) are independent, sufficiently small feasible \(d\) must be zero.

The obstruction extends to an entire boundary-pinned rectangular patch. Take the sites \(iu+jv\), \(0\le i,j\le m\), fix its boundary, and let \(t\) be the largest displacement of an interior site. Telescoping the unit-separation inequalities along the original \(u\)\- and \(v\)\-rows yields

\[
|u\cdot d_{ij}|,\ |v\cdot d_{ij}|\le 2mt^2.
\]

The least singular value of the matrix with rows \(u^T,v^T\) is \(\sqrt2\sin(\theta/2)\). Therefore

\[
t=0
\quad\text{or}\quad
\boxed{t\ge\frac{\sin(\theta/2)}{2m}.}
\tag{4}
\]

So **there is no nonzero sufficiently small boundary-pinned collective deformation**, despite the absence of unit triangles and the presence of full nearhex cells.

### 4\. Diameter stress can coexist with triangle-free contacts

The unit square is an exact global minimizer for \(n=4\), with \(D^2=2\) and no unit equilateral triangle.

Give weight \(1/2\) to each of its two diameter pairs and weight \(1/2\) to each of its four unit sides. These weights satisfy the complete first-order equilibrium equations, including

For every fixed \(n\), take any exact unrestricted global minimizer \(X\). Perturb its coordinates generically so that all pairwise distances become distinct, then rescale its shortest distance to one.

The resulting configurations have exactly **one unit contact**, hence no unit triangle, and their diameters converge to \(D_n\). Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\inf_{\substack{|Y|=n,\ \min\operatorname{dist}(Y)=1\\
Y\text{ has no unit }K_3}}
\operatorname{diam}(Y)=D_n.
}
\tag{5}
\]

The infimum need not be attained.

This rules out any proposed universal positive diameter gap between all triangle-free feasible configurations and the unrestricted optimum. A charge argument must exploit **exact attainment and variational stability**, rather than nearoptimal density alone.

### 6\. Exact-global finite-\(n\) stress test

Bezdek and Fodor proved

\[
D_8=\frac1{2\sin(\pi/14)}.
\]

Take a regular unit-side heptagon and add its center. The heptagon attains this diameter; its circumradius \(r=1/(2\sin(\pi/7))>1\).

The center may move anywhere in the open ball of radius \(r-1\) without violating separation or changing the diameter. Hence there is a continuous family of **exact unrestricted global eight-site minimizers** with a contact-free interior site and no unit \(K_3\).

This is only a small-\(n\) exception, but it confirms that exact globality alone does not enforce local contact activation.

### 7\. Minimal missing implication and next test

The missing step is a **boundary-inclusive second-order release theorem** for triangle-free, nearhex configurations.

A concrete certificate to search for is a pair of displacement fields \(v_i,a_i\), producing

\[
x_i(t)=x_i+t v_i+\tfrac12t^2a_i.
\]

For every active unit pair \(e=ij\), require

\[
e\cdot(v_i-v_j)=0,\qquad
\|v_i-v_j\|^2+e\cdot(a_i-a_j)>0.
\]

For every active diameter pair \(f=ij\), require

\[
f\cdot(v_i-v_j)=0,\qquad
\|v_i-v_j\|^2+f\cdot(a_i-a_j)<0.
\]

These strict inequalities guarantee that sufficiently small positive \(t\) preserves all original separations and **strictly reduces the diameter**.

The next falsifiable lemma I recommend testing is:

This would exclude the canonical four-contact, six-facet, triangle-free lattice mechanism from exact global optimality. A counterexample satisfying first- and second-order stationarity would refute the proposed lemma, without necessarily refuting Erdős #99.

## 1. Sharp angular gap for disjoint diameter segments — independently verified, historically established

**Earlier sources:** [pinned 9 September 2026 sharp disjoint-diameter theorem](https://github.com/1337isnot1337/erdos-99/blob/b05cd57b15252fe99577de3edb0b73070e79544f/docs/reports/target_c_disjoint_diameter_angle_2026-09-09.md) and [pinned independent outer-walk sequel](https://github.com/1337isnot1337/erdos-99/blob/b05cd57b15252fe99577de3edb0b73070e79544f/docs/reports/target_c_disjoint_diameter_gap_outerwalk_collapse_2026-09-09.md). Worker `w60_496_disjoint_db_gap` reconstructed the sharp bound. Earlier `w59_465` derived a correct weaker bound. The original project has priority for the sharp result relative to this continuation; no claim of external historical novelty.

**Lemma.** If a planar finite set has all pair distances in `[1,D]` and `AB,CE` are vertex-disjoint diameter-D pairs, the acute angle `theta` between their unoriented directions obeys

`theta >= 4 arcsin(1/(2D))` (for the relevant large-D range).

**Independent proof.** Write diameter vectors `u,v` with acute angle `theta`, and set `p=(u-v)/2`, `q=(u+v)/2`; these are perpendicular with norms `r=D sin(theta/2)` and `R=D cos(theta/2)`. If `w=(alpha,beta)` is the midpoint displacement expressed in unit axes along `p,q`, the four cross-pair vectors are `w±p,w±q`. Diameter constraints `|w±q|<=D` give `|beta|<=D-R`. Unit separation of the other two cross pairs yields

`1 <= min(|w+p|²,|w-p|²)=(r-|alpha|)²+beta² <= r²+(D-R)² = 4D² sin²(theta/4)`.

Taking the inverse sine gives the bound. The proof needs *all four distinct endpoints*, but neither KKT optimality nor absence of equilateral triangles. For `D>=(1+sqrt5)/2` equality is realized by the four points `U±=(±D/2,H)` and `V±=(±(D-1/D)/2,0)`, `H=sqrt(1-1/(4D²))`: the two sloping diagonals have length D, both legs have length 1, top horizontal length D, bottom horizontal length `D-1/D>=1`, and the diagonal acute angle equals `4asin(1/(2D))`.

**Executed check:** [audit-wave62-angles-heptagon.py](../work/erdos99/audit-wave62-angles-heptagon.py) verified all six pair distances and angular equality at `D=golden ratio,2.5,3,9,100,10^6`. The million-scale double-precision angle displays expected floating-point cancellation at `~2e-11` absolute error; the analytic proof supplies exact equality. Existing source [59 difference-body audit](https://github.com/1337isnot1337/erdos-99/blob/b05cd57b15252fe99577de3edb0b73070e79544f/docs/targets/target-c/59-difference-body-density-audit.md) used only universal `2asin(1/(2D))` direction gaps, so the sharp stronger *disjoint* result is compatible with it.

**Attribution:** worker `w60_509_reinhardt_capacity`; ROOT independently checked the coefficient arithmetic and full all-label competitor comparison, using classical [Oler 1961 finite packing inequality](https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1961-018-7), the isodiametric inequality, and elementary translated triangular-lattice averaging. **Theorem (independently reconstructed from workers w63_553 and w63_555).** Fix constants `0<A_min<=A_max<infinity` and `ell>0`. Uniformly over planar lattices `Lambda` of fundamental area `A` satisfying `A_min<=A<=A_max`, minimum nonzero lattice-vector length at least `ell`, translations of those lattices, and convex planar sets `K` of diameter at most `D`,

    |Lambda intersect K| <= pi D^2/(4A) + o(D),       D -> infinity.

The uniform `o(D)` is an *upper* error. This includes every translated unit rhombic lattice generated by unit vectors at angle `theta` in `[pi/3,2pi/3]`, with `A=sin(theta)>=sqrt(3)/2`. Thus, using the separately established global minimum-diameter population reserve

    n >= pi D^2/(2sqrt(3)) + D/600 + 1,             D >= 10^6,

no sufficiently large **globally** minimum-diameter original `n`-point configuration can have **all** labels on any single such unit rhombic lattice. It is enough that every label lies on the lattice; the contact graph need not use every unit edge. This does **not** say that the selected positive-stress vertices, an isolated chamber, or each grain individually cannot lie on a lattice.

**Root proof.** Put `S=Lambda intersect K`, `P=conv(S)`. Convexity gives `Lambda intersect P=S`. If `P` is degenerate, `|S|<=D/ell+1` (or at most one point). Otherwise it is a lattice polygon. By Pick's formula, letting `B` be its number of lattice points on its boundary,

    |S| = area(P)/A + B/2 + 1.

For every maximal straight polygon edge `e=m_e v_e` with primitive lattice direction `v_e`, `m_e` is a positive integer, `|v_e|>=ell`, and `B=sum_e m_e<=per(P)/ell<=pi D/ell`. Suppose the asserted uniform upper `o(D)` failed: for a sequence `D_j -> infinity`, some uniform epsilon>0 would satisfy

    |S_j| >= pi D_j^2/(4A_j) + epsilon D_j.

Pick, the perimeter bound, `A_j<=A_max`, and isodiametry imply the area deficit `Delta_j=pi D_j^2/4-area(P_j)` satisfies `0<=Delta_j=O(D_j)`. Normalize by `D_j` and translate one vertex to the origin. Any Hausdorff-convergent subsequence of these diameter-at-most-one bodies has area `pi/4`, hence by equality in the planar isodiametric theorem is a disk of radius `1/2`. Consequently the maximal polygon edge length `L_j=o(D_j)` **uniformly along any putative violating sequence**: otherwise a macroscopic supporting side survives in a disk limit, impossible.

For a fixed cutoff `R>ell`, lattice separation bounds the number of primitive direction vectors of length `<R` by `N_R<=(1+2R/ell)^2`, uniformly over the lattice family. A convex polygon has at most two maximal edges in each unoriented direction. The short-primitive edges contribute at most `2N_R L_j/ell` boundary steps; long-primitive edges contribute at most `per(P_j)/R<=pi D_j/R`. Therefore

    B_j/D_j <= 2N_R L_j/(ell D_j) + pi/R.

First `j->infinity`, then `R->infinity`: `B_j=o(D_j)`. Pick and isodiametry now yield `|S_j|<=pi D_j^2/(4A_j)+o(D_j)`, contradicting the fixed `epsilon D_j` surplus. Assume the numerical population reserve

    |P| >= pi D^2/(4 a0) + D/600 + 1.

For **every** translated/rotated unit triangular lattice `Lambda`, at least `2D` **original points** of `P` are *off* `Lambda` and lie at Euclidean distance **strictly less than 10** from `boundary(K)`. No selected-core or physical-stress assumption occurs in this theorem. Its premise holds for sufficiently large global minimum-diameter sets **assuming** the separately established 15 October original-label population-reserve result.

**Independent proof, including endpoint and double-counting checks.** Let `K_{-w}={x in K: dist(x,boundary K)>=w}` and `S_w=K\K_{-w}`. If the inner parallel body is nonempty, then `diam(K_{-w})<=D-2w`: the radius-`w` closed disks about two of its points lie inside convex `K`, and their opposite extreme points along the common connecting line are separated by `|x-y|+2w`. The bound is trivial if `K_{-w}` is empty. Oler's finite packing inequality, the isodiametric inequality and the Cauchy perimeter bound thus give

    |P intersect K_{-w}| <= pi(D-2w)^2/(4a0) + pi(D-2w)/2 + 1

for `D>2w`; taking the difference with the population reserve gives, for `N_w=|P intersect S_w|`,

    N_w >= [pi*w/a0 - pi/2 + 1/600] D - pi*w^2/a0 + pi*w.                 (1)

This includes boundary points correctly: `S_w` is *strict* depth `<w`, and `K_{-w}` is closed depth `>=w`.

Choose unit triangular basis `u,v` at angle 60 degrees. The index-three sublattice `Lambda_0=<u+v,2u-v>` has determinant magnitude 3 in the `(u,v)` basis. Its cosets partition **all** lattice sites once into the disjoint triangles `{z,z+u,z+v}`, with `z` ranging through `Lambda_0` (plus the lattice's common translation). A direct residue proof: the `(u,v)` site `(i,j)` lies in coset `i-j mod 3`; the three vertices of each triple give residues `0,1,2`. A triangle-free `P` occupies at most two vertices of any triple.

These triangles' centroids form a triangular lattice of covolume `3a0` and shortest distance `sqrt(3)`. Its Voronoi hexagons have area `3a0` and circumradius `1`; a triangle vertex is distance `1/sqrt(3)` from its centroid. Consequently, with `R=1+1/sqrt(3)`, whenever a triple meets any measurable set `S`, its centroid's **entire** Voronoi cell is contained in `S+B_R`. Disjoint Voronoi interiors therefore prove

    |P intersect Lambda intersect S| <= [2/(3a0)] area(S+B_R).            (2)

In particular, `S_w+B_R` lies inside `K+B_R` and outside `K_{-(w+R)}`. The inner-strip area is bounded by `(w+R) per(K)` via inner-parallel coarea and convex perimeter monotonicity; the outer parallel area adds `R per(K)+pi R^2` by Steiner. Since `per(K)<=pi D`, (2) yields

    |P intersect Lambda intersect S_w|
       <= [2pi/(3a0)](w+2R) D + 2pi R^2/(3a0).                           (3)

The difference of (1) and (3) counts *distinct original off-lattice labels*, exactly once:

    |(P\Lambda) intersect S_w|
       >= [pi(w-4R)/(3a0) - pi/2 + 1/600] D
           - pi*w^2/a0 + pi*w - 2pi R^2/(3a0).                           (4)

The script additionally checked the index-three partition on 625 nearby lattice sites. This is a **restricted structural consequence** of classical Oler and the stated reserve, not a contradiction. It does **not** imply that the off-lattice labels are hull vertices, carry positive contact stresses, occupy empty area, or incur a diameter penalty. ## 3. Triangle-free configurations have the same diameter infimum

**Root-checked elementary lemma, not a solution.** For each `n>=2`, let `D_n` be the smallest diameter of a unit-separated `n`-point planar set. The infimum restricted to configurations with *no equilateral triple at any side length* is also `D_n`, even if the restricted configurations are required to have minimum pair distance exactly 1.

Proof: compactness after pinning one vertex supplies an optimizer `P`; its minimum separation equals 1 or a uniform contraction improves it. For `t>=0`, apply `A_t=diag(1+t,1)`. For a fixed labeled triple, two different `t` making it equilateral would force all three squared horizontal pair differences equal. Three real numbers with all mutual distances equal must coincide, making the triple collinear and never equilateral. Thus each triple forbids at most one `t`, so a sequence `t_j>0`, `t_j->0`, avoids all finitely many forbidden parameters. Put `m_j=minsep(A_{t_j}P)` and `Q_j=A_{t_j}P/m_j`. Then `1<=m_j<=1+t_j`, `minsep(Q_j)=1`, no `Q_j` contains an equilateral triple, and

    D_n <= diam(Q_j) <= (1+t_j)D_n.

The full conjecture concerns **actual attainment** at exactly `D_n`; a triangle-free global optimizer at small `n` (for example a unit square at `n=4`) is consistent with this lemma. A positive gap between the two diameter *infima* is impossible for any `n`.

## 4. Convex hull near-disk stability with an explicit constant

**Root-checked convex-analytic lemma (worker `w65_594_uler_oler_area_neardisk_stability`).** For compact convex planar `K` of diameter `D=2R`, deficit `E=pi R^2-area(K)`, some center `c` satisfies

    d_H(K, closed_disk(c,R)) <= E/(pi R) + sqrt(3E/(2pi)).             (6)

Proof: translate to the Steiner point and expand the support function as `h(theta)=m+sum_{j>=2}(a_j cos(j theta)+b_j sin(j theta))`, with `m=per(K)/(2pi)<=R`. The convex support-area identity

    area(K)=pi*m^2 - (pi/2) sum_{j>=2}(j^2-1)(a_j^2+b_j^2)

is valid for nonsmooth convex bodies by `H^1` support-function approximation. Thus the weighted sum is at most `2E/pi`. Cauchy–Schwarz and the *exact* telescoping sum `sum_{j>=2}(j^2-1)^{-1}=3/4` imply `||h-m||_infinity<=sqrt(3E/(2pi))`. Moreover `E>=pi(R^2-m^2)>=pi R(R-m)`, so `R-m<=E/(pi R)`. For convex bodies, Hausdorff distance is the uniform distance between support functions, proving (6). This also holds for polygons.

The Oler inequality on the **original** convex hull and the 15 October global reserve imply `E<=C D` with `C=(sqrt(3)/2)(pi/2-1/600)<1.36`. Equation (6) yields `d_H<=sqrt(3C/(2pi))*sqrt(D)+2C/pi <0.806*sqrt(D)+0.866`. The exponent `1/2` cannot be improved from area deficit alone: the convex constant-width support function `h(theta)=R+t cos(3theta)` for `0<t<=R/8` has diameter `2R`, deficit `4pi t^2` and Hausdorff deviation proportional to `t` from any radius-`R` disk. These are exact **geometric** statements and give no strict improvement of exact unit contacts.

## A. Quantitative local hexagonality of almost densest **original** point sets

**Source and credit:** Browser worker `w66_620_all_labels_grain_partition`, 28 October 2026, supplied the saturation/Voronoi argument. Root independently checked its finite counting, compactness, equality case, and original-versus-auxiliary point bookkeeping. The local Voronoi area inequality itself is classical; for a modern self-contained proof and exact equality characterization see A. Mazel, I. Stuhl, Y. Suhov, *Minimal Area of a Voronoi Cell in a Packing of Unit Circles* (2022), https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.03255. The source's separation-two cell bound `2 sqrt(3)` rescales to `a=sqrt(3)/2` at separation one.

Let `P` be a unit-separated original planar set with convex hull `K`, diameter `D`, perimeter `L`, and

    n = |P| >= (pi/(2 sqrt(3))) D^2 + D/600 + 1.                  (R)

Choose a cardinality-maximal unit-separated finite superset `Q` of `P` **inside the fixed original K**. Compactness and disjoint half-unit disks guarantee existence. `Q` covers `K` at distance **strictly less** than one, since a point at distance at least one could otherwise be added. With `t=|Q|-n`, Oler and the isodiametric bound give

    0 <= t <= L/2 - D/600 <= pi D/2.                             (1)

Separate Q centers into `I` at distance >=1 from ∂K and boundary centers `B=Q\I`, count `b`. A full-plane Voronoi cell of `q in I` is contained in the closed radius-one disk about q: if not, a segment from q toward a farther cell point crosses the unit circle inside K, giving a feasible new center at distance >=1 from all of Q. The classical cell bound then gives `area(V_q)>=a`; equality requires the regular hexagonal cell with six exact unit neighbors. Disjoint radius-1/2 disks at the b boundary centers lie inside the width-3/2 tube around ∂K, of area at most `3L+9pi/4`; therefore

    b <= 12L/pi + 9 <= 12D+9.                                    (2)

All interior cells are contained in K, and their total area excess `E=sum_{I}(area(V_q)-a)` is nonnegative. The uncovered part `R_K=area(K)-sum_I area(V_q)` is nonnegative. Consequently

    E+R_K = area(K)-a(n+t-b)
          <= a(b-t-D/600-1) <= a(12D+8).                          (3)

For fixed `0<epsilon<=1/20`, define an interior center to be epsilon-good if it has six distinct Q neighbors with vectors within epsilon of a rotated regular unit hexagon. There exists `delta_epsilon>0` such that any bounded radius-one Voronoi cell failing this condition has excess area at least `delta_epsilon`. Proof: sites within distance two determine the radius-one cell, and at most 25 unit-separated sites lie in the radius-two disk by area comparison. The configurations form a sequentially compact finite union (with labels chosen after a subsequence). Boundedness passes to the limit because the halfspace family contains the fixed radius-half disk. Voronoi area is continuous under these constraints. Vanishing excess would force the unique regular-hexagonal equality configuration and hence six epsilon-near vertices, contradicting failure. The modulus is existence-only; no numerical value is claimed.

At most `a(12D+8)/delta_epsilon` centers in I are bad. Exclude original centers in B, all bad centers, and every original center within distance 2 of a newly added Q\P site. Each new site has <=25 centers within radius 2, so at least `n-Z_epsilon` **original** points have six **original** near-unit neighbors, where

    Z_epsilon = 12D+9 + a(12D+8)/delta_epsilon + 25 pi D/2.     (4)

Consecutive-neighbor triples have all sides in `[1,1+2epsilon]`. Six triples arise around each good original center; each can be counted at most three times, so the original P contains at least `2(n-Z_epsilon)` distinct near-unit equilateral triples. For the graph of original edges of length `<=1+epsilon`, maximum degree is <=6 (seven near neighbors create an angular gap <=2pi/7 and hence a distance <1). At most `6Z_epsilon` short edges meet an exceptional original center. Adjacent good centers' local hexagonal orientations agree modulo pi/3 within `2 arcsin(epsilon)`.

**Scope caution:** An O(D) **graph-edge exception count** is not a bound on physical grain boundary length, the number of global orientations, or exact unit-equilateral triangles. Good orientations can drift across long paths. The theorem is conditional on (R), valid for the original labels, and does not itself use global optimality except through that reserve. A unit rhombic lattice with angle `pi/3+eta`, `eta>0` arbitrarily small, has nearly regular Voronoi cells and zero unit equilateral triples; exactness cannot be extracted from an O(D) aggregate excess without an additional global argument.

## D. Eliminating fully inactive original labels by changing the optimizer

**Source and credit:** Worker `w66_634_global_optimal_contact_degree` supplied this elementary argument. Root independently checked the finite generic-ray construction and the convex-hull extremality claim. This is a **representative-existence** statement and must not be applied to *every* global minimizer.

Let P be a global unit-separated n-point minimum-diameter configuration with D>1. Call p *fully inactive* if all its distances to the other labels are strictly between 1 and D. Hold all other labels fixed and move p along a generic ray until the first equality `|p-q|=1` or `D`. At least one occurs since distant points eventually violate the upper bound; until then all distances obey both constraints. Avoiding finitely many crossing directions ensures precisely one new equality, so if a unit contact appears, p has just one and cannot complete a unit triangle. All old tight pairs persist. Global optimality ensures the resulting feasible configuration still has diameter D. Repeat; the process stops after at most n steps with every label incident to a unit contact or diameter pair, preserving triangle-freeness if P was triangle-free.

Every diameter endpoint is an extreme hull vertex by strict convexity of squared distance. A hull with m vertices has perimeter at least m (consecutive original vertices separated by >=1), while its perimeter is at most pi D. Hence **some** global optimizer `P*`, chosen from a given P and retaining all its old tight pairs, has at most `pi D` **original** contact-isolated labels; if P was triangle-free, P* remains so. The argument neither bounds the stress-positive core nor forces contacts to lie in triangles, and does not prove the original requested all-optimizer conjecture.

    delta=pi*D^2/4-A.

Assume the *pinned, unreviewed* 15 October original-label population reserve

    n >= pi*D^2/(2*sqrt(3)) + D/600 + 1.                 (R)

Oler's inequality `n<=A/a0+p/2+1`, combined with `p<=pi D`, gives

    0<=delta<=C0*D.                                      (1)

Translate by the Steiner point so the first support Fourier harmonics vanish. With `h(theta)=a+sum_{k>=2}(a_k cos(k theta)+b_k sin(k theta))`, the support-function identity (valid for polygonal K, by the absolutely continuous support and area representation) yields

    p=2*pi*a,
    A=pi*a^2-(pi/2)*sum_{k>=2}(k^2-1)*(a_k^2+b_k^2),
    delta=pi*(R^2-a^2)+(pi/2)*sum_{k>=2}(k^2-1)*(a_k^2+b_k^2).

Since `a<=R`, all terms on the right are nonnegative and `R-a<=delta/(pi*R)`. Thus

    0<=pi*D-p <=4*delta/D <=4*C0 <5.44.                (2)

Further, Cauchy–Schwarz and `sum_{k>=2}1/(k^2-1)=3/4` imply `sup|h-a|<=sqrt(3*delta/(2*pi))`. Hence the Steiner-centered hull lies between concentric disks with radii `R +/- M_D`, for

    M_D = 2*C0/pi + sqrt(3*C0*D/(2*pi)) = O(sqrt(D)).  (3)

For the longest hull edge of length `ell`, consider `L=(K-K)/2`. By Brunn–Minkowski `area(L)>=A`; by the diameter bound `L` lies in `B(0,R)`. The edge of K produces a face of L of length **at least ell/2**. A disk cap cut by a chord of length `s` has area >=`s^3/(12R)` (differentiate the circular-segment formula: derivative >=`s^2/(4R)` and integrate from zero). Consequently

    delta >= pi*R^2-area(L) >= ell^3/(48*D),
    ell <= (48*C0)^(1/3)*D^(2/3).                      (4)

For a fixed sector about the Steiner point with angle `beta in (0,pi)`, rays at its endpoints intersect K at radial distance at least `R-M_D` for large D. Their boundary points have chord length at least `(D-2*M_D)*sin(beta/2)`. The polygonal boundary arc between them uses edges of length at most (4), so at least

    (D-2*M_D)*sin(beta/2) /
       ((48*C0)^(1/3)*D^(2/3)) - 1                      (5)

**hull vertices inside the sector**, up to the obvious endpoint convention. This is `Omega_beta(D^(1/3))` *original* hull vertices. It says nothing about exact unit contacts: individual consecutive hull gaps can still grow as `D^(2/3)`.

## 2. Multigrain lattice crops: an exact seam identity and conditional population inequality

**Credits:** Browser researcher `w66_626_TypeII_interface_perimeter` (28 Oct 2026) supplied this *conditional* theorem and constants. This root independently reconstructed the counting and optimization. Pick's theorem dates to Georg Pick (1899); Oler's convex packing inequality is from 1961. Earlier project report **31 August** already studies internal-face cancellation, and **11 October** has related lattice boundary estimates; no first-discovery claim is made here.

Let K be the convex hull of an original unit-separated n-point set P of diameter D>=1. Suppose K is tiled by m positive-area **convex lattice polygons** G_i with disjoint interiors, each G_i having vertices in a translated lattice Lambda_i of minimum vector length at least one. Put `S_i=G_i intersect Lambda_i`, `v_i=covolume(Lambda_i)>=a0`, and let `e=|P\(union S_i)|` (thus `P subset (union S_i) union E`; union crops may contain extra sites). Let `U` count *represented* sites on internal grain boundaries belonging to exactly one crop; sites shared by two crops are not in U. Define the nonnegative lattice density loss

    L_loss = sum_i area(G_i)*(1/a0-1/v_i) >=0.

**Exact identity.** For a boundary site x represented in `t(x)` of the S_i, Pick's theorem on each convex **lattice** polygon gives

    |union_i S_i| = sum_i area(G_i)/v_i + m
                     + sum_{x in union_i (boundary G_i intersect Lambda_i)}
                              (1-t(x)/2).            (6)

Proof: `|S_i|=area(G_i)/v_i+B_i/2+1`, and a boundary point counted t times must have `t-1` copies subtracted. Hence its net correction is `t/2-(t-1)=1-t/2`. An internal seam site with t=2 contributes exactly zero; a site seen in just one grain contributes +1/2; triple intersections contribute negatively. Writing B_ext for represented sites of the outer boundary, (6) implies

    n <= sum_i area(G_i)/v_i + m + (B_ext+U)/2 +e.   (7)

This requires **true shared physical sites** for cancellation: adjacent geometrical grain edges or matching orientations alone do not suffice.

**Boundary estimate.** Set `delta=pi D^2/4-area(K)>=0`. The cap argument from section 1 works without global optimality and bounds every hull edge by `(48 D delta)^(1/3)`. On a unit-separated lattice, disjoint radius-1/2 disks bound the number of nonzero vectors of length at most T (T>=1) by `9T^2`; summation by parts then bounds the sum of their inverse lengths by `18T`. In any convex lattice polygon of diameter at most D, count edges by primitive directions: at most `9 D^(2/3)` edges with primitive length <=`D^(1/3)` and at most `pi D^(2/3)` longer ones by perimeter. Thus each grain has fewer than `13 D^(2/3)` vertices. For the external part of its edges, count represented sites of short primitive length at most T by the inverse-length sum and the hull-edge bound; long directions contribute at most `pi D/T` globally (external exposed segment interiors are disjoint). Hence

    B_ext <= 13*m*D^(2/3) + 18*m*T*(48*D*delta)^(1/3)
              + pi*D/T.                                (8)

Substituting `sum_i area(G_i)/v_i = pi D^2/(4a0) - delta/a0 -L_loss` into (7), using `(48)^(1/3)<4` and `a0<1`, we need maximize `-z^3+36*m*T*D^(1/3)*z` over `z=delta^(1/3)>=0`. Its maximum is `48*sqrt(3)*m^(3/2)*T^(3/2)*D^(1/2)`. If `m<=D^(1/3)`, choose `T=(D/m^3)^(1/5)>=1` and note `48*sqrt(3)+pi/2<85`, `13/2<7`. The result is

    n <= pi D^2/(2sqrt(3)) + U/2 + e - L_loss
         +85*m^(3/5)*D^(4/5) +7*m*D^(2/3) +m.        (9)

This is a theorem about **all original labels** only under the very demanding *exact whole-crop grain representation* hypothesis. It is not proved that arbitrary global optimizers admit such a decomposition.

If P is also a global minimizer satisfying the pinned reserve (R), subtraction gives the necessary condition

    U+2e >= D/300 +2 +2*L_loss
             -170*m^(3/5)*D^(4/5)-14*m*D^(2/3)-2m. (10)

For `m=o(D^(1/3))`, the error is `o(D)`, so `U+2e >= (1/300-o(1))*D`. This excludes a small-number-of-grains complete-crop global optimizer with `U+e=o(D)`; it does **not** exclude polycrystals with linear unmatched seam counts or linearly many original sites outside crops. A strong theorem that additionally controlled U, e, or converted their size to a strict global diameter improvement would still be needed.

## 4. Stronger fixed-hull saturation obstruction from wave67

**Credit:** Browser researcher `w67_648_Oler_equality_classification` (28 Oct 2026) supplied the explicitly all-original parallelogram example; root reconstructed the algebra and checked representative cases. This is an *independent alternative to* the earlier triangular-chamber obstruction from w66_625. It is not a globally minimum-diameter example.

For any integer M>=1 and any prescribed eta>0 choose theta>pi/3, so close that 0<M^2(2 sin(theta)/sqrt(3)-1)<min(eta,1/2). Let u=(1,0), v=(cos(theta),sin(theta)), P={i*u+j*v: 0<=i,j<=M}, K={s*u+t*v:0<=s,t<=M}. Then K is a convex parallelogram, n=(M+1)^2, area M^2 sin(theta), perimeter 4M, and P is unit separated. Indeed every lattice displacement (a,b) has squared length a^2+b^2+2ab cos(theta). If ab>=0, all nonzero squared lengths are at least one; if ab<0, the squared length is strictly larger than a^2+b^2-|ab|>=1. Thus the only unit vectors are +/-u and +/-v, and no unit equilateral triangle exists (|u-v|>1, |u+v|>1).

For any *arbitrary* unit-separated Q subset K, Oler and monotonicity of convex area and perimeter imply |Q|<=area(K)/a0+perimeter(K)/2+1 = n+sigma, with 0<sigma<1/2. By integrality |Q|<=n. Hence P exactly maximizes cardinality among all unit-separated subsets of **its same convex hull**, even when Q is not lattice based and every point is allowed to move. The absolute Oler slack can be made arbitrarily small for every M. Choosing theta_M=pi/3+1/(100 M^3) yields slack O(1/M)->0 as M->infinity, while P remains triangle-free.

This rules out the implication “arbitrarily tight Oler saturation plus fixed-hull population optimality forces an exact unit triangle.” It still leaves open the stronger *global same-n minimum diameter* property demanded by Erdős #99. Root code in work/erdos99/audit-wave68-hull-multigrain.py verifies slack/integer contacts for M=1,2,10,100,1000 and finite displacement enumeration for M<=10 (PASS). The separate worker discussion of a Graham–Witsenhausen–Zassenhaus 1972 exact-equality characterization was not independently source-refereed here, so no reliance is placed on it.

## 5. Pell bicrystal: exact finite seam count and an UNCONDITIONAL strict competitor

**Credit:** Browser researcher `w67_642_multi_grain_cut_interface` (28 Oct 2026) supplied the rational Pell two-grain family, its exact row-count identity, and the disk-lattice discrepancy argument. Root independently checked the all-label finite counts and sharpened the non-globality conclusion by **a strict same-n smaller-diameter competitor that needs no unreviewed project reserve**. Script `work/erdos99/audit-wave69-pell.py` PASS. This is an exclusion for this specific candidate family, not a proof of the general Erdős conjecture.

Take coprime odd integers q>p>=3 satisfying q^2-3p^2=-2, e.g. (q,p)=(5,3),(19,11),(71,41),(265,153). Set M=q^2+p^2, c=(q^2-p^2)/M=1/2-1/M, s=2pq/M=sqrt(1-c^2)>sqrt(3)/2, R=M/2. Define original *physical* two-grain points

    P_left  = {(i+c*j,s*j): i,j integers, x<=-1/2, x^2+y^2<=R^2},
    P_right = {(i-c*j,s*j): i,j integers, x>=+1/2, x^2+y^2<=R^2},
    P       = P_left union P_right.

Each component lattice has min separation one and unit directions only horizontal and its one diagonal, so no unit triangle. Between grains horizontal distance >=1; a cross-grain unit pair would be horizontal across the gap, and the third vertex of its potential equilateral triangle would have x=0, which P excludes. Points (+/-R,0) are included, so actual original diameter of P is exactly M.

Let J=floor(M^2/(4pq)). The complete left generating lattice Lambda+ has exactly 2J+1 occupied rows in B_R. Because M is even with c of odd reduced denominator, every row has exactly one lattice site in the open strip |x|<1/2; all these sites lie in B_R (at the end rows, W_J^2>=2(M^2-2)>M^2/4). Left and right crops are reflected and rows +j/-j must be paired: their aggregate count is the full lattice count in the two rows minus **two** (the loss need not be one in *each* row). The zero row loses one. Therefore the exact integer identity is

    |P| = |Lambda+ intersect B_(M/2)| - (2J+1).          (11)

This was checked directly by independent integer-coordinate radius tests and `isqrt` for M=34, 482, 6722, and 93634, yielding (full, physical two-grain, removed) respectively (1031, 992, 39), (210355, 209800, 555), (40974489, 40966728, 7761), and (7951028055, 7950919936, 108119). The attempted stronger per-row-one-loss assertion FAILED on j=-18 at M=34; after correcting to paired rows, all exact tests PASS. No observed failure of the worker's actual identity.

The relevant basis matrices and inverses form a uniformly bounded family (c between 8/17 and 1/2, s bounded below). The standard smoothed Poisson-summation disk estimate is therefore *uniform* in the family: for R large,

    N_Lambda+(R)=pi R^2/s+O(R^(2/3)).

For completeness, convolve disk indicators of radii R +/- t with a compact mollifier supported in B_t; radius error O(Rt); at nonzero dual frequencies the disk transform R*J_1(2pi R|xi|)/|xi| and |J_1(z)|=O(z^(-1/2)) yield O(R^(1/2) t^(-1/2)) uniformly because the dual lattices are uniformly separated. Choose t=R^(-1/3). Since s=sqrt(3)/2+1/(sqrt(3)M)+O(M^(-2)) and 2J+1=M/s+O(1), equation (11) gives

    |P| = pi M^2/(2sqrt(3)) - ((pi+6)/(3sqrt(3)))*M
           + O(M^(2/3)).                                  (12)

**New direct strict competitor (unconditional):** For any fixed 0<epsilon<(pi+6)/(6pi), take a unit triangular lattice of covolume a0=sqrt(3)/2 and translate it uniformly over one fundamental cell. The *mean* number of lattice points in the disk B_(R-epsilon) is exactly

    pi(R-epsilon)^2/a0
       = pi M^2/(2sqrt(3))-(2pi*epsilon/sqrt(3))*M+O(1).

By the strict epsilon inequality, its mean exceeds the candidate |P| by a positive multiple of M for all sufficiently large Pell solutions, using (12). Therefore **some translation** contains at least |P| sites in that smaller disk. Choose exactly |P| of them: they remain unit separated and have diameter at most M-2epsilon, strictly below the candidate's actual diameter M. In particular epsilon=2/5 gives a diameter improvement of at least 4/5 for sufficiently large members. This argument relies on elementary Fubini translation averaging and the independently reconstructed uniform disk discrepancy, **not** the project-specific October 15 reserve. Numerically, the exact finite counts show the mean surplus for epsilon=2/5 is positive at all four audited M (7.62, 195.74, 2038.39, 29320.46).

This eliminates the particular Pell two-grain exact phase model as an infinite family of globally diameter-optimal triangle-free counterexamples. It does not cover arbitrary two-grain seam phases, boundary reconstructions, or global optima with inactive off-lattice labels. Root does not claim a whole-problem proof.

## 1. Unconditional original-label approximate hexagons (worker w68_655; stronger verification of w66_620)

Let `P` be a globally minimum-diameter unit-separated set, `n=|P|`, `D=diam(P)`, `K=conv(P)` with nonempty interior, `A=area(K)`, `a=sqrt(3)/2`. For each fixed epsilon>0 there is an explicitly defined `delta_epsilon>0` such that at most

`H_epsilon <= (8+8a/delta_epsilon)D + 1`

**original** sites fail to have six **original** distinct neighbors lying within epsilon of a rotated unit regular hexagon. Consequently P contains at least `2n-2H_epsilon` distinct original unordered triples with all sides in `[1,1+epsilon]` (choose eta<=epsilon/3). No project October 15 linear population reserve is used.

**Root proof.** Translate the unit triangular lattice uniformly modulo its fundamental domain. A disk of radius `r<D/2` has mean `pi*r^2/a` sites; since `P` is globally optimal, every such translate has at most `n-1` sites, otherwise select n and get smaller diameter. Letting `r` increase to `D/2` yields `n>=pi*D^2/(4a)+1>=A/a+1`; write `d=n-A/a>=1`.

Take a maximum-cardinality unit-separated extension `Q superset P` **inside K**, of size `n+M`. It is saturated in K: every x in K has `dist(x,Q)<1`. Let `B` count Q sites within distance 1 of boundary K. Their disjoint radius-1/2 disks lie in `(K+B_{1/2}) \ K_{-3/2}`. Convex parallel-set formula and coarea for inner offsets give area <= `2per(K)+pi/4`, so `B<=8per(K)/pi+1<=8D+1` (Cauchy `per(K)<=pi D`).

Any Q-site q deeper than distance 1 in K has its **whole-plane** Voronoi cell V_Q(q) contained in B(q,1): if a radial segment within this cell first reached radius 1, its endpoint lies inside K and has another Q-site at distance <1 by saturation, contradiction. Thus these `n+M-B` bounded cells lie disjointly inside K. Historical sharp Voronoi inequality (Mazel–Stuhl–Suhov 2022 after rescaling unit disks to unit-separated centers) states `|V|>=a` with equality precisely for the regular hexagon. Hence their total nonnegative excess E obeys

`E = sum (|V_Q(q)|-a) <= A - a(n+M-B) = a(B-M-d)`.

For any fixed eta>0, among bounded cells contained in B(q,1), there is `Delta_eta>0` such that if its center does not have six Q-neighbors within eta of a unit regular hexagon, its cell excess is >=Delta_eta. To prove positivity, use only Q-neighbors within distance 2: those sites determine the bounded central cell. There are <=19 sites including the center in the radius-2 disk by **Bateman–Erdős 1951 Theorem 2**, directly checked in the primary PDF, printed p306. Compactness of at most 19 unit-separated sites in a fixed disk, continuity of bounded Voronoi-cell area, and the exact hexagonal equality characterization give positive Delta_eta. Choose eta=min(epsilon/3,1/10), delta_epsilon=min(Delta_eta,a/18)>0.

At most `b<=a(B-M-d)/delta_epsilon` deep original sites have bad local Q-neighbor configurations. Every auxiliary site in Q\P can contaminate at most 18 original centers within radius 2 (again Bateman–Erdős). At most B originals lie within the boundary band. Therefore `H<=B+b+18M<=B+(a/delta_epsilon)(B-d) <=(8+8a/delta_epsilon)D+1`. Six near-regular original neighbors at each good center define six distinct near-unit triples; any unordered triple is counted by at most three centers, so at least `2(n-H)` distinct triples.

**Verification limitations.** No numerical closed form for the stability modulus. The compactness argument applies to the full bounded cell: any Q-site beyond distance 2 cannot remove an already interior unit-radius Voronoi boundary point, so distant sites are irrelevant. This is entirely approximate and cannot imply an exact unit triangle. \[n\ge \pi D^2/(4a)+1.\tag{4}\]

# Erdős #99 — wave75: exact six-sided original Voronoi certificates

## A. Facet-contact equality

Let `P` be any finite unit-separated planar configuration. Suppose an **original** site `p` has bounded ordinary Voronoi cell `V_p` with exactly six nondegenerate facets, corresponding to distinct **original** neighbors `q_1,...,q_6`. Let `d_i=|q_i-p|>=1`, `ell_i>0` be the length of the associated facet, and `A=area(V_p)`, `L=perimeter(V_p)`.

    4*A - L = sum_(i=1..6) ell_i*(d_i-1) >= 0.            (A1)

Proof: with origin at `p`, the outward unit normal of the i-th facet is `(q_i-p)/d_i`, its support distance is `d_i/2`, and the divergence theorem gives `2A = sum_i(d_i/2)*ell_i`. Subtract `L=sum_i ell_i` to obtain (A1). If `4A=L`, every `d_i=1` because each `ell_i>0`. Six distinct mutually unit-separated original points lie on the unit circle centered at `p`; their successive angular gaps are at least 60 degrees, sum to 360 degrees, and therefore all equal 60 degrees. Consecutive original neighbors, together with `p`, form exact unit equilateral triples.

## B. Pure area certificate and nonnegative geometric defects

Let successive outward facet normals have gaps `alpha_i in (0,pi)`, with `sum alpha_i=2pi`. Move all six bisector support lines inward to distance `1/2` from `p`, retaining normal directions, and call the tangential hexagon `T_p`. It is contained in `V_p`. Its area is `A(T_p)=1/4*sum_i tan(alpha_i/2)`. Consequently the **exact** identity is

    A - sqrt(3)/2
      = [A - A(T_p)]
        + (1/4)*[sum_i tan(alpha_i/2) - 2*sqrt(3)].     (B1)

Both terms are nonnegative: containment gives the first, while Jensen's inequality applied to strictly convex `tan` on `(0,pi/2)` gives `sum tan(alpha_i/2)>=6*tan(pi/6)=2sqrt(3)`. If `A=sqrt(3)/2`, both vanish. Equality in Jensen makes all angular gaps exactly 60 degrees, and equality of the nested convex polygons makes all six support distances `1/2`. ## Theorems and proof

Let `P={p_1,...,p_n}` be an unrestricted **global** diameter-minimizing unit-separated packing with `n>=3` and two-dimensional hull `K`. Among all global minimizers choose one maximizing `J(P)=sum_{i<j}|p_i-p_j|^2`. This maximum exists: translate `p_1` to the origin; diameter `D=D_n` bounds all other coordinates, and the feasible equality-diameter minimizer set is compact. Write `T` for the original sites incident to an actual diameter-`D` pair, `F=P\T`, `m` for hull vertices and `b` for all original sites on the hull boundary.

**A. All original hull-boundary sites are actual diametral endpoints in a J-maximizer; `T=vert(K)` and `t=m=b`.** Suppose `p` is an original boundary site absent from `T`. Choose an outward unit supporting normal `v` with `(p-q)·v>=0` for all original `q`. Displace just `p` to `p+eps v`. Distances from `p` to all other original sites are weakly *increased*: the squared-distance change is `2eps(p-q)·v+eps^2>=eps^2`. Originally inactive upper distances incident to `p` have positive finite slack since `p∉T`, so remain strictly below `D` for all sufficiently small `eps>0`. An original diameter pair not involving `p` remains fixed, hence the new configuration still has diameter exactly `D`, and is globally optimal. But every squared distance from `p` increases strictly, so `J` increases, a contradiction. Therefore all boundary originals belong to `T`. Every diameter endpoint is an extreme vertex of `K`: if `p` lies in the relative interior of `[u,w]` with `u,w∈K` and `|p-q|=D`, strict convexity of `|·-q|^2` gives `max(|u-q|,|w-q|)>D`; represent `u,w` as convex combinations of original sites to contradict `D`. Hence `T⊆vert(K)⊆boundary originals⊆T`, so **`t=m=b`**. In particular no original J-maximizer site lies in the relative interior of an original hull edge. The boundary selection argument is inspired by the same J tie-break used by previous root §215 and worker `w73_757`; an earlier, **different** lexicographic perimeter/margin selection already forced hull vertices to be diametral (`w68_660`, canonical §200). No historical novelty is asserted.

## B. A maximum principle for positive-stress unit-contact components

**Provenance:** browser worker `w73_772_global_contact_topology` supplied the particular harmonic-support observation and the derived perimeter/area inequality. ROOT independently rederived the component maximum principle and Oler/Reinhardt consequence below. Earlier full stress method and related structural reductions are in **Archit Das (2026)**, *Stress, rigidity and rhombic reductions for an Erdős minimum-diameter problem*, 15 September 2026 preprint, DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22768362; see also prior project canonical §219 (`w73_773`). No novelty over Das or classical discrete maximum principles is asserted.

For any original local (hence global) minimizer, KKT supplies nonnegative weights `lambda_ij` on exact unit pairs and `mu_ij` on exact diametral pairs, with `sum mu=1`, `sum lambda=D^2`, and site equilibrium `sum_j lambda_ij(p_i-p_j)=sum_j mu_ij(p_i-p_j)`. The constraint qualification is explicit: the direction `(dot p_i=p_i, dot t=3t)` strictly improves all active pair inequalities in the squared-diameter program. Let `B` be the set of original sites incident to **positive** mu stress, and `S` the sites incident to **positive** lambda stress. For each connected component H of the positive-lambda graph,

`V(H) subset conv(B intersect V(H))`.

**Proof.** At every site not in B, the weighted contact equilibrium is `p_i = (sum_j lambda_ij p_j)/(sum_j lambda_ij)` with strictly positive denominator. The scalar projection on any fixed line is therefore a graph-harmonic function at every non-B site. A maximum among finite H vertices can occur at a non-B vertex only if all its positive-neighbor projections share the same maximum; connectivity propagates until reaching B. If no B exists in H, both coordinate projections would have to be constant on H, contradicting that each contact edge has positive length. Every support functional on `conv(V(H))` therefore achieves its maximum on `B intersect V(H)`, proving containment. In particular an ORIGINAL extreme hull vertex without a positive diametral multiplier must have zero positive-contact multipliers.

The whole stressed set obeys `conv(S) subset conv(B)`. Write `U=n-|S|`, and let m be the number of vertices of `conv(B)`, if m>=3. Because B inherits diameter<=D, Oler's unit packing bound and the convex perimeter bound yield `n-U <= (2/sqrt(3))*area(conv(B)) + pi D/2 +1`. By the **strict translated-lattice global competitor argument**, `n>=pi D^2/(2sqrt(3))+1`. The classical diameter-D polygon area bound attributed to Reinhardt gives `area(conv(B)) <= (m D^2/2)*(sin(pi/m)-tan(pi/(2m)))`. Hence

`U >= (D^2/sqrt(3))*[pi/2-m(sin(pi/m)-tan(pi/(2m)))]-pi D/2`.

The bracket is `5pi^3/(24m^2)+O(m^-4)`. Therefore, if U<=CD throughout a family, then `m >= (sqrt(5pi^3/(24sqrt(3)(C+pi/2)))-o(1))*sqrt(D)`. This is conditional on a sufficiently populated **positive-stress** region; no existing theorem rules out U much larger than D for arbitrary GLOBAL optimizers. It is a structural dichotomy, not an exact-triangle theorem. ## A. Sharp global bound for the ORIGINAL triangle-free unit-contact graph

**Source of this formulation:** browser worker `w74_786_circular_annulus_packing`, section 4, local saved result `work/erdos99/w74_786_circular_annulus_packing.result.json`. ROOT independently rederived the claim below and checked its often-missed disconnected and isolated cases. The Euler/planarity method itself is classical; earlier canonical project section around line 1829 already used `e<=2v-2-b/2` for a *selected connected component*. No historical priority assertion is justified for the unrestricted entire-original-graph formulation.

Let A be any finite **original-site** unit-separated planar set with n>=3 noncollinear sites, **no three forming an exact unit equilateral triangle**, and convex hull K. Let E comprise pairs at distance **exactly** one, let e=|E|, and let b=|A intersect boundary(K)|, including collinear boundary sites. Then

`e <= floor(2n-2-b/2)`.                                               (A1)

**Independent proof.** Unit-length contact segments cannot cross transversely: from a transverse intersection choose a closer endpoint of each segment, each at distance <=1/2 from the crossing; the two distinct selected endpoints are at distance strictly <1. So the simple original contact graph is planar. Split it into k connected components with sizes `v_i`, edge counts `e_i`, and outer-face boundary-walk lengths `l_i` (each bridge traversed twice). Every bounded face has boundary-walk length >=4: a three-step closed walk in a simple graph would be a 3-cycle and hence an exact unit equilateral triangle. Euler and double-counting incidences give `2e_i >= 4(e_i-v_i+1)+l_i` and therefore `e_i <= 2v_i-2-l_i/2`. For an isolated component `v_i=1,e_i=l_i=0`, this inequality is equality. Let s be the number of isolated components. Every site of A on the *global* convex-hull boundary that belongs to a nontrivial component must appear on that component's outer-face boundary walk (a supporting line through it keeps the graph on one side). Every isolated global-boundary site contributes at most one of s. Hence `b <= sum_i l_i+s`. Summation yields `e <= 2n-2k-(b-s)/2`; since `2k-s/2>=2` whenever n>=3, (A1) follows, including all disconnected/isolated cases. Integrality supplies the floor.

**Sharpness without globality.** An m-by-m unit square grid patch has `n=m^2`, `b=4m-4`, and `e=2m(m-1)=2n-2-b/2`. Its contact graph is triangle-free. This is sharp as a bound on feasible triangle-free original contact graphs, not an example of an unrestricted *global* minimum-diameter packing.

Since each original unit-contact degree is at most 5 when exact unit triangles are absent, (A1) also gives the exact discharging identity/inequality

`sum_{d=0}^3 (4-d) N_d >= N_5 + b + 4`,                       (A2)

where `N_d` counts original sites with d unit contacts. It forces low-degree compensation for every five-contact site. Combining b>=h with the already ROOT-audited unconditional GLOBAL hull-vertex estimate (canonical section 210, browser `w70_699`/ROOT Wave73) produces

`e <= 2n-2-(0.7704313427...-o(1))*sqrt(D)`                    (A3)

along any family of triangle-free original *globally minimum-diameter* packings with D tending to infinity. This is the existing hull result's coefficient `sqrt(5*pi^2/(12*sqrt(3)))/2`; it improves worker `w74_786`'s weaker `0.689...` coefficient based on a less sharp hull count. It remains only an **upper** contact bound and does not imply a unit triangle.

## A. A definitive degree-two countercheck to extrapolating site-local SOS

**Credit:** Browser referee `w75_796_three_site_sos_referee`, saved at `work/erdos99/w75_796_three_site_sos_referee.result.json`, found the obstruction; root independently derived the full algebra and computed the rational witness. The original *correctly restricted* k-site injection argument was supplied by `w73_764_nonlinear_sos_geometry`, root-checked and recorded in canonical §221 / Wave79. This is a scope clarification, **not** a correction to that already precise §221 statement. Background SOS notions: https://www.sumofsquares.org/public/lec-definitions-general .

Let k≥2 anchors `a_1,...,a_k` be pairwise distinct feasible points; choose a vector `u` with nonconstant projections, and put `z_r=u·a_r - (sum_s u·a_s)/k`. Let `sigma²=(1/k)sum_r z_r²>0`. For every set of ≤k labeled variables, define its joint moments by uniform **injections** of those labels into the k anchors. These marginals agree on overlaps. For distinct label indices i,j,

```
E[Z_i]   = 0,
E[Z_i²]  = sigma²,
E[Z_i Z_j] = (sum_{r≠s} z_r z_s)/(k(k-1))
            = -sigma²/(k-1),
where Z_i = u·x_i - (sum_r u·a_r)/k.
```

For **n>k**, these pair marginals uniquely determine the expectation of the explicitly global degree-one polynomial `Q=sum_{i=1}^n Z_i` squared:

```
E[Q²] = n sigma² - n(n-1) sigma²/(k-1)
      = n(k-n) sigma²/(k-1) < 0.
```

This proves that the consistent local injections **cannot** be a positive semidefinite global degree-two moment functional (its n-by-n covariance matrix has a negative eigenvalue along the constant vector). The exact smallest displayed witness uses k=3, n=4, anchors `(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)`, projection `u=(1,0)`: `z=(-1/3,2/3,-1/3)`, `sigma²=2/9`, `E[Z_i Z_j]=-1/9` for distinct indices, and `E[Q²]=-4/9`. Root independently evaluated these rational numbers via Python `fractions.Fraction`, PASS.

**Valid retained result:** Uniform injections witness nonnegativity of each FULL SOS square or inequality localizer involving **jointly at most k distinct site labels**, at any polynomial degree. They say nothing against a global SOS term mixing more than k labels even if its expansion consists of low-support monomials. Do not extend the scoped §221 no-go to unrestricted global SOS. This adversarial check defeats that tempting extension.

## B. New triangle-free-preserving monotone normal form for **selected descendants**

**Credit:** Browser worker `w75_800_hull_jmax_fixed`, `work/erdos99/w75_800_hull_jmax_fixed.result.json`, §§3–4 proposed the contact-deletion algorithm. Root independently checked its three phases below against all pair constraints. The earlier arbitrary J-max representative hull-endpoint and pinned-rank properties are already in canonical notes (do **not** claim first discovery). The precise improvement is that the new procedure begins with *any* original global optimum, introduces **no** new exact unit contacts, and therefore carries an assumed triangle-free global optimum to a triangle-free globally optimal normal form. No historical originality claim is made.

**Proposition.** Let `P=(p_1,...,p_n)` be any noncollinear, globally minimum-diameter, unit-separated planar configuration, diameter `D`, n≥3. There exists a configuration `Q=(q_1,...,q_n)` with the same n and **same globally minimal diameter** D, such that, identifying pairs by the same labels,

1. Its exact unit-contact set `C(Q)` is a subset of `C(P)` (no new unit edges).
2. Every site on the boundary of `conv(Q)` is an actual endpoint of a diameter-D pair.
3. Every connected component of the exact unit-contact graph with at least one edge intersects that hull boundary.
4. On the interior sites incident to an exact unit edge (omitting contact-isolated sites), the contact rigidity matrix with all hull boundary sites pinned has full column rank `2(n-h-z)`, where `h` denotes boundary-site count and `z` the number of contact-isolated interior sites.

In particular, if `P` has no original exact equilateral unit triangle, neither does `Q`. This says nothing about whether the *original* P already satisfies 2–4.

**Phase I, boundary normalization.** If a boundary site `p_i` is not a diameter endpoint, select an outward supporting normal `u` at `p_i`, so `u·(p_i-p_j)≥0` for every other site. Move only `p_i` to `p_i+t u`. Every incident squared distance is `|p_i-p_j|²+2t u·(p_i-p_j)+t²`, strictly increasing for t>0; nonincident distances remain fixed. Move until the **first** previously subdiametral pair incident to i reaches D. That finite positive time exists because incident lengths eventually exceed D, while none equals D initially. The moved point is now a diameter endpoint, all previous diameter endpoints stay such, all lower pair bounds hold, and no unit contact is created. An endpoint of an actual diameter pair is an exposed hull vertex (the standard squared-distance expansion gives a unique maximizing direction), so repeating increases the number of diameter endpoints and terminates after at most n moves. At termination, all boundary sites are diameter endpoints.

**Phase II, unanchored components.** Fix this hull polygon. If a contact component W contains an edge but no boundary site, all W sites are strictly interior. Expand their positions by factor `1+epsilon` around their centroid, leaving all other labels fixed. For sufficiently small epsilon>0, W remains inside the original hull. Its internal pair lengths strictly increase, thereby deleting its exact unit edges. All cross-pairs were *strictly* greater than 1 because W was a contact component; finiteness supplies a small enough epsilon to preserve these inequalities without creating contacts. All sites stay in the same diameter-D hull, and the diameter pair of pinned hull endpoints persists. Each such move decreases `|C|` and preserves global optimality and boundary normalization.

**Phase III, infinitesimal pinned flex.** Pin the boundary sites and contact-isolated interior sites. Suppose the contact rigidity matrix restricted to the remaining interior columns has nonzero kernel v. Then `(p_i-p_j)·(v_i-v_j)=0` on every unit edge, with v=0 on pinned labels. Because every nontrivial contact component reaches a pinned boundary site, at least one unit edge has `v_i≠v_j` (otherwise the velocity would be constant and zero throughout each nontrivial component). Move the unpinned sites along `p_i+t v_i` for sufficiently small nonzero t. Every old unit edge has squared length `1+t²|v_i-v_j|²≥1`; at least one is **strictly** longer. Previously noncontact edges stay greater than 1 by positive finite slack. Interior sites remain in the fixed convex hull, all upper diameter constraints hold, and a pinned hull diameter pair persists. Thus a positive integer number of exact contacts disappears, none appears. Repeat phases II–III; each move strictly decreases the finite contact count, so termination yields the claimed pinned full column rank and no floating nontrivial components.

This proof handles hull-edge-interior sites by the same exposed-vertex argument; isolated interior sites are explicitly excluded from the rank statement. n≥3 global optima are noncollinear (a collinear n-site unit-separated set has diameter ≥n−1 while simple bent competitors have smaller diameter). No assumption about the original contact graph's connectivity, stress positivity, or a positive diameter gap is used.

**Why this cannot yet solve #99.** A counterexample P is transformed into a possibly different counterexample Q. The full rank only supplies `e(Q)≥2(n-h-z)` and does not force a 3-cycle in the triangle-free contact graph; isolates can be numerous. Prior Euler `e≤2n-2-h/2` is compatible with this lower bound. The original problem quantifies over every actual original optimizer, which this descendant normal form does not characterize. A new uniform global bound on isolates or an all-optimizer contact theorem remains missing.

## B. An explicit triangle-free *unrestricted global* eight-site minimizer

Set `theta=pi/7`, `R=1/(2 sin theta)`, `v_j=R(cos(2j theta),sin(2j theta))`, `j=0,...,6` and `H=conv{v_j}`. Adjacent sides are `2R sin theta=1`, the longest heptagon diagonal has length

`2R sin(3pi/7)=2R cos(pi/14)=1/(2 sin(pi/14))=D_8`.

The center is inside `H` and `R=1.15238243548124...>1`; thus `P_0={v_0,...,v_6,0}` is unit separated, its exact unit-contact graph is just the boundary 7-cycle, and **it has no unit equilateral triangle**. ## C. All maximizers of the convex tie-breaker have a unit triangle

Let `a=R cos theta`, `r=a-sqrt(3)/2=0.172235294501729...>0`, and for `j mod 7` set

`w_j = r(cos((2j+1)theta),sin((2j+1)theta))`.

Each `w_j` lies inside `H`, on the inward normal of side `[v_j,v_(j+1)]`. The adjacent separation is exactly

`|w_j-v_j|^2 = |w_j-v_(j+1)|^2 = (1/2)^2+(sqrt(3)/2)^2=1`.

All its other vertex separations exceed one. Thus each heptagon plus `w_j` is another **globally optimal** eight-point set, now with exact original unit triangle `{w_j,v_j,v_(j+1)}`.

**Key exact feasible-set lemma.** Let `F={p in H: |p-v_j|>=1 for all j}`. Then

`conv(F)=conv{w_0,...,w_6}`.

Proof: write `rho=|p|<=R`. For `rho>0` at least one vertex has polar separation from `p` at most `theta`. Its squared distance is at most `g(rho)=R^2+rho^2-2a rho`. Direct substitution gives `g(r)=1`, while

`g(R)=2R^2(1-cos theta)=1/[4 cos^2(pi/14)]<1`.

As `g` is convex, `g(rho)<1` throughout `r<rho<=R`, since its graph lies below the chord from `(r,1)` to `(R,g(R))`. Hence every `p in F` satisfies `|p|<=r`. Write `u_j=v_j/R` and use `|p-v_j|^2>=1` to obtain

`p·u_j <= (R^2+|p|^2-1)/(2R) <= (R^2+r^2-1)/(2R) = r cos theta`.

The intersection of these seven supporting halfplanes is exactly the regular heptagon `conv{w_0,...,w_6}` (whose outward side normals point along `u_j`). All seven `w_j` themselves lie in `F`, proving the lemma. Equality in the radial bound `|p|<=r` is possible only when its nearest vertex has polar gap exactly `theta`, forcing `p=w_j` for some `j`.

Since `sum_j v_j=0`, the natural tie-breaker

`J(P)=sum_(i<j)|p_i-p_j|^2`

has, for an eight-point optimizer with heptagon hull and free eighth point `p`, the form

`J({v_j} ∪ {p})=C+7R^2+7|p|^2`, with `C` depending only on the seven hull vertices. Therefore **every** `J`-maximizing *unrestricted global eight-point optimizer* has `p=w_j` and a unit equilateral triangle. More generally, by the convex hull lemma, every maximizer of a strictly convex function of the eighth point, keeping this heptagon fixed, belongs to `{w_j}`: convexity and the strict inequality rule out nonvertex convex combinations. The global statement about `J` uses the full hull-classification theorem.

This gives a precise counterexample to the tempting *general* transfer `there exists a triangle-free global optimizer ⇒ there exists a triangle-free J-max global optimizer`. It does not refute a hypothetical **eventual large-n** version of the transfer or Erdős #99.

`sup{J(P): P is triangle-free and globally optimal at n=8}=max{J(P): P is globally optimal at n=8}`,

## A. Original-hull Oler slack cannot vanish for `n >= 336` (ROOT verified)

Let `X` have `n >= 3` unit-separated sites, nondegenerate convex hull `K`, perimeter `P`, area `A`, diameter `D`, and Oler slack

`S = 2A/sqrt(3) + P/2 + 1 - n >= 0`.

If `S=0`, apply Graham–Witsenhausen–Zassenhaus, *On tightest packings in the Minkowski plane*, Pacific J. Math. 41 (1972), Theorem 5, pp.714–715 (https://msp.org/pjm/1972/41-3/pjm-v41-n3-p10-p.pdf). The convex-hull triangulation can use the **original vertices** and consists entirely of unit equilateral triangles. Its hull boundary has turns in positive integral multiples of `pi/3`, hence at most six strict vertices. By the polygonal isoperimetric inequality, `A <= sqrt(3) P^2/24`. Cauchy's perimeter–diameter inequality gives `P <= pi D`. Therefore zero slack forces

`n <= P^2/12 + P/2 + 1 <= pi^2 D^2/12 + pi D/2 + 1`.

Averaging translations of the unit triangular lattice over a disk of radius `R` yields some translate containing at least `pi R^2/(sqrt(3)/2)` original lattice sites. Thus `D_n^2 <= (2 sqrt(3)/pi)n` (any `n` of those sites give a valid unrestricted comparison). Substituting `D=D_n` entails

`(1 - pi sqrt(3)/6)n <= sqrt(pi sqrt(3) n/2) + 1`.

The left side minus the right side is positive at `n=336` and strictly increasing thereafter; `335` is not excluded by this particular numeric argument. Independently checked with explicit rational enclosures `pi<355/113`, `sqrt(3)<86603/50000`, `pi sqrt(3)<54415/10000` and monotonicity in `work/erdos99/audit-wave85-native.py` (PASS). Hence **every unrestricted global minimizer for `n>=336` has `S>0`**. This excludes the proposed route of forcing *exact* equality in Oler globally, but does not establish the existence or absence of a unit triangle in the global optimum.

## E. Second-order pinned-flex Farkas criterion (ROOT algebra audit)

Historical worker `w76_819_original_disk_hole_exchange` gives a valid finite strict-linear feasibility test. For a first-order feasible velocity field `v`, let `L_ij(v)=(p_i-p_j)·(v_i-v_j)`; define zero-derivative contacts `C_0={c∈C:L_c(v)=0}` and diameter pairs `H_0={h∈H:L_h(v)=0}`. Quadratic trajectories `p_i(t)=p_i+t v_i+t² a_i/2` satisfy the exact squared-length expansion with coefficient `L_ij(a)+|v_i-v_j|²` at `t²`. Strict second-order descent follows if `L_c(a)+|Δv_c|²>0` for every `c∈C_0` and `L_h(a)+|Δv_h|²<0` for every `h∈H_0`.

For normalized nonnegative equilibrium stresses supported on `C_0,H_0` with `Σ_h μ_h=1` and `Σ_c λ_c L_c(w)=Σ_h μ_h L_h(w)` for every `w`, define `Q_v=Σ_c λ_c |Δv_c|²-Σ_h μ_h|Δv_h|²`. Applying Farkas to the non-strict strengthened inequalities with common margin `δ>0` gives feasibility **if and only if** `Q_v >= δ(Σλ+Σμ)=δ(D²+1)` for every such stress. A contact-only nonzero equilibrium stress is impossible because substitution `w_i=p_i` gives `Σλ=0`. Thus, by compactness, strict feasible accelerations exist exactly when the normalized stress set is empty or its minimum `Q_v` is strictly positive. ROOT checked all inequality signs, normalization and the compactness step directly.

At every local diameter optimum, an original first-order KKT stress is supported on `C_0,H_0` (complementarity against first-order feasible `v`), so the stress set is nonempty and `min Q_v <= 0`. This is a **necessary** second-order condition and a **sufficient** strict-quadratic descent test, not a claim that every possible higher-order descent must appear at quadratic order. In particular, triangle-free contacts do not force a violating velocity `v`. Standard Farkas/KKT methods have historic priority; no literature novelty asserted.

Wave87 `w87_859_nonlinear_rooted_lifting` (job `5f828023-67d6-42bd-ab35-b25ece0f84b4`) correctly observes that *arbitrary* two-degenerate contact graphs cannot protect an uncompressed diameter pair: the exact unit square has two mutually crossing diameters. Reverse removal order: every nonroot site has at most two contact neighbors already present. This argument remains valid for disconnected graphs and after removals because they are themselves penny graphs.

Therefore **every triangle-free local diameter minimizer with (D>1) has at least two distinct original diametral pairs**. P_K\ge\pi\left(\sqrt{D^2+\frac34}-\frac{\sqrt3}2\right).

Therefore \(I=\int_0^\pi(D-w(\theta))\,d\theta=\pi D-P_K<\pi\sqrt3/2\).
At almost every direction, choose opposite supporting points of \(K\) separated by a vector of norm at most \(D\). Differentiating the support functions gives

\[
|w'(\theta)|\le\sqrt{D^2-w(\theta)^2}
\le\sqrt{2D(D-w(\theta))}.

Consequently \(\sqrt{D-w(\theta)}\) is \(\sqrt{D/2}\)-Lipschitz on the circle of directions (period \(\pi\)). If \(M=\max(D-w)\), integrate its necessary triangular lower envelope of width \(\sqrt{2M/D}\) around a maximizer:

\[

\]

Since \(M\le D\), the envelope's total support width is at most \(2\sqrt2<\pi\) and its integration is valid. Combining inequalities yields the **pointwise original-global theorem**

\[

\left(\frac{3\pi\sqrt3}{4\sqrt2}\right)^{2/3}D^{1/3}
>D-2.027D^{1/3}\quad\text{for all }\theta.}
\]

The last bound uses \(c=2.026925767547617\ldots<2.027\), audited in `audit-wave89-root.py`. ## 4. Second-order nonlinear compression as a sufficient strict-descent test

James derived a precise stress-dual sufficient condition. On a given original unit-separated configuration let \(E\) contain **all** exact unit-contact edges and \(F\) **all** exact diameter edges. A normalized equilibrium stress consists of nonnegative \(\lambda_e\) and \(\mu_f\), satisfying vertexwise force balance, \(\sum_F\mu_f=1\) and \(\sum_E\lambda_e=D^2\). The normalization follows by dotting equilibrium with the original positions. For any velocity vector \(v=(v_i)\) with

\[
(p_i-p_j)\cdot(v_i-v_j)=0\quad\text{for all }ij\in E\cup F,
\]

define \(Q_\sigma(v)=\sum_E\lambda_e\lVert v_i-v_j\rVert^2-\sum_F\mu_f\lVert v_i-v_j\rVert^2\). If **every normalized equilibrium stress** has strictly positive \(Q_\sigma(v)\) (equivalently, its minimum over the compact stress polytope is positive), then an elementary Farkas-separation argument supplies accelerations \(a_i\) with strict second-order opening of every unit contact and strict closing of every diameter edge. The path \(p_i(t)=p_i+t v_i+\tfrac12t^2a_i\) gives a feasible, original-label, **same-n configuration of strictly smaller diameter** for sufficiently small positive \(t\).

The proof uses \(\sum\lambda=D^2\sum\mu\) to rule out nonzero contact-only or diameter-only dual obstructions; all inactive constraints have a strictly positive finite margin. At a local optimum, the contrapositive says that for every such velocity \(v\) there exists a normalized equilibrium stress with \(Q_\sigma(v)\le0\). This is a **necessary structural test**, not the missing claim that every triangle-free global optimizer admits a violating \(v\).

As a stringent example, the (triangle-free, non-global) \((m+1)\times(m+1)\) unit square grid, \(m\ge2\), is strictly compressed by

\[
(i,j)\mapsto
\left(i\left(1-\frac38t^2\right),
j\left(1+\frac18t^2\right)+t g_i\right),
\qquad
g_i=\begin{cases}i,&i<m,\\0,&i=m.\end{cases}
\]

All original unit contacts increase in length to second order; both original diameters decrease in squared length by \(\frac12m^2t^2+O(t^4)\). Inactive constraints retain slack for sufficiently small \(t\). ROOT checked **all pairs exactly with Python rational fractions** for \(m=2,3,5,10\), not just an expansion. This improves the explicit grid witness but is not an argument for arbitrary global optimizers.

Native Lovelace independently proposed a simpler sufficient criterion: if a first-order stationary velocity \(v\) has \(\min_{e\in E}\|\Delta v_e\|^2>\max_{f\in F}\|\Delta v_f\|^2/D^2\), global scaling by \(1-ct^2\) for a strictly intermediate \(c\) produces the same kind of strict descent. \[
